newsitem.title: EGYPT: Pricing method dims demand for Egyptian selloff.
newsitem.headline: Pricing method dims demand for Egyptian selloff.

text.p: Confusion over a pricing method for the Egyptian state's offer of 40 percent in General Silos and Storage has dimmed investor demand but the offering is covered, the agent for the sale said on Wednesday.

"Demand has been limited because investors don't understand the new system. They think its a trap but this leaves the way for the investors who really understand what's going on and are serious," said Nadir Ezzedine at the National Bank of Egypt.
He told Reuters the new computerised system enabled the state and investors to arrive at a price for the four million shares.
The state has priced the stock at a minimum of 37 pounds and allocated two million to individuals and one million each to financial institutions and the company's employee shareholder association.
"Initial results show that the offering has been covered," he added. The two-day share offering ended on Tuesday but the final share price might be available on Sunday.
The privatisation is the first for about a month and marks the start of an accelerated programme in which the state expects to sell 91 companies by the middle of 1998.

The state does not intend to sell more than 40 percent, regardless of demand, because General Silos works in what the state considers a strategic sector -- the storage and transport of wheat for subsidised bread.

The firm's financial department head told Reuters earlier the company made net profits of 48.3 million pounds in the financial year 1995/6, compared with 40.489 million in 1994/5 and 32.992 million in 1993/4. The years end on June 30.
The company is forecasting net profits of 43.485 million pounds in the current year and 61 million in 1997/8. For last year it will pay a dividend of at least 3.35 pounds, he said.
